Kong/Nginx/Spring Cloud Gateway/Pingora

Comparison Dimension Kong Nginx Spring Cloud Gateway Pingora
Core Architecture Based on OpenResty (Nginx + Lua) Native C development, event-driven model Built on Spring 5 + Reactor (reactive programming framework) Rust-based, multi-threaded async architecture, memory-safe design
Protocol Support HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, gRPC (with modules), TCP/UDP HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, WebSocket HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, gRPC
Performance ~5k-10k QPS per node (depends on plugin complexity) ~50k-100k QPS per node (pure proxy scenarios) ~10k-20k QPS per node (limited by Java ecosystem) 400k+ QPS per node (Cloudflare-tested), <1ms latency, 2x Nginx throughput
Configuration Declarative (YAML/DB), Admin API Static config file (nginx.conf) Java code or YAML (Spring Boot integration) Dynamic config (API/config files)
Plugin/Extensibility Rich plugin ecosystem (100+ official/community plugins: auth, rate limiting, logging) Modular extensions (requires compiling/dynamic modules), flexible but high dev cost Custom Filters/GlobalFilters, relies on Spring ecosystem New plugin system (Rust extensions), limited ecosystem
Use Cases Microservices API gateway, enterprise traffic management High-performance reverse proxy, Layer 7 load balancing, static caching Lightweight API gateway in Spring ecosystems Edge computing, ultra-high-performance proxy, cloud-native, large-scale traffic
Community & Support Active OSS community + Enterprise (Kong Konnect) Large OSS community + Commercial (Nginx Plus) Maintained by Spring, integrated with cloud providers (e.g., AWS) Open-sourced by Cloudflare, enterprise support via Cloudflare ecosystem
Key Limitations Database dependency (PostgreSQL/Cassandra), complex clustering Dynamic config requires third-party modules (e.g., Lua), limited modern protocol support JVM performance limits, high plugin dev cost Immature ecosystem, limited docs, HTTP-focused protocols

Summary & Recommendations

  1. Ultra-High Performance Needs

    • Prioritize Pingora (e.g., CDN, edge computing) or Nginx (pure proxy scenarios).

  2. Microservices & Ecosystem Integration

    • Kong (rich plugins) or Spring Cloud Gateway (Spring ecosystem users).

  3. Simple Proxy & Static Config

    • Nginx (mature, low resource usage).

  4. Enterprise Features & Support

    • Kong Enterprise or Nginx Plus (paid subscriptions).
